script: Cheat on your wife with mine? I will burn your life to the ground. . Way back in the early 2000s, I started getting the weird vibe that my wife was hiding something. The kids were only 4 and 6, still bright enough to spill secrets, but the way they kept saying they were staying with her parents during the day made me pause. 90 minutes away? They did it two or three times a week, even on days she wasn't working. But here's the thing… I started tracking her mileage, and boom—400 extra miles a week. She wasn't just running errands. What I didn't know was that she was driving all those hours to a place that wasn't on any map. And that's when everything changed. One night, while I was scrolling through my old AOL account, I saw a sticky note on her keyboard: her password. I couldn't resist. I logged in, opened her inbox, and found a thread with her college BFF talking about how she'd been hooking up with an ex-boyfriend from high school. No specifics, just trash talk about his wife being "fat" after kids. I printed the emails, taped them to my notebook. But here's the thing… I called a buddy who used to be a cop, and he suggested I reach out to a PI he knew—Ron, the guy who had left the force to dig up dirt. I paid the retainer, handed him the emails, and asked him to find out what was going on. What I didn't know was that Ron had a knack for turning a mystery into a full-blown dossier. And that's when everything changed. Ron's report was like watching a car crash in slow motion. He mapped out every trip: the kids to her parents, lunch with a guy at a dingy motel, then back home. He included photos, dates, times, locations. My heart hit the floor. But here's the thing… I hired a divorce lawyer because my parents' messy marriage had already wrecked our family. If this didn't work, I'd lose my sanity and my kids. What I didn't know was how deep the web of deceit was. And that's when everything changed. Ron dug deeper and found the guy's name—Bob. He was a VP of sales, married with three kids, and his wife was a quiet, kind woman. He worked for his father-in-law's business, which owned the house they lived in. The audacity! But here's the thing… I got the divorce papers drafted, and I asked Ron to meet Bob's wife with the evidence. He did, and she looked stunned. I thought she'd just file for divorce. What I didn't know was that she would take matters into her own hands. And that's when everything changed. She emptied the joint account, took the kids, and left. Bob got fired when his boss found out. The house was evicted because it was owned by his in-laws. The divorce became a war: restraining orders, police reports, even jail time. I felt like a bystander at a hurricane. But here's the thing… I could barely find Bob online now. He vanished, leaving the state, while his ex-wife took over at her dad's company. The whole saga ended like a bad reality show finale—no happy ending. What I didn't know was how this would shape my kids' view of trust. And that's when everything changed. Now, I and my ex keep it strictly business. No drama, just the kids. I don't hate her; I just care about their well-being. The past is a closed file, and the future is bright. I keep my best friend vibes with them, and that's the final tea.
